title: Real-Time Multi-Entity Consolidation Without Waiting on Close
summary: Real-time multi-entity consolidation without close means consolidated financials as activity posts, with automated eliminations. See how Flow Agentic Accounting Platform differs from QBO spreadsheets.
body_markdown:
Real-time multi entity consolidation without close is what CFOs mean when they say, “I need the group P&L before the board deck, not after we finish eliminations.” Traditional close treats consolidation as a batch event. Modern multi-entity ERPs keep a consolidated view current as entities post, with eliminations applied continuously.


## Key takeaways


Use these points when leadership asks for live group numbers.


-


**Meaning:** Real-time consolidation produces consolidated financials from live entity data without waiting for a month-end consolidation “run.”


-


**Prerequisite:** Multiple entities in one instance (or a live consolidation layer) plus identifiable intercompany activity and automated eliminations.


-


**QBO pattern:** Separate company files push consolidation into spreadsheets after each entity closes, the opposite of real time.


-


**Flow Agentic Accounting Platform:** Real-time consolidation and automated eliminations on a one-instance multi-entity ledger; LiveFlow FP&A offers live consolidation when you stay on QBO.


## What does “consolidation without close” actually mean?


It does not mean skipping controls, bank recs, or period lock. It means the *group view* is not hostage to a once-a-month consolidation workbook.


In a real-time model:


-


Entity activity posts to a shared multi-entity ledger (or streams live into a consolidation layer)


-


Intercompany balances are visible as they arise


-


Automated eliminations keep consolidated revenue, expense, and reciprocal BS accounts clean


-


Leadership can open a consolidated P&L or balance sheet mid-period for decision-making


You still close the period for statutory and audit purposes. You stop pretending the only trustworthy consolidated number appears on working day eight.


For the accounting process backdrop, see[consolidating financial statements](https://www.liveflow.com/blog/consolidating-financial-statements) and[consolidated financial reporting](https://www.liveflow.com/blog/consolidated-financial-reporting) .


## Why spreadsheet consolidation can never be truly real-time


On QuickBooks Online, each entity is a separate company file. Consolidation usually looks like:


1.


Wait for each entity’s books to be “done enough.”


2.


Export trial balances or P&Ls.


3.


Map accounts in Excel or Google Sheets.


4.


Enter elimination journals in the workbook.


5.


Refresh charts for the board.


Every step is a snapshot. A late AP bill in Entity C does not appear until someone re-exports. That is why controllers hesitate to send “draft consolidated” numbers mid-month: the process itself is batch-oriented. Detail on that workflow:[consolidating multiple entities in QuickBooks Online](https://www.liveflow.com/blog/consolidating-multiple-enitities-in-quickbooks-online) .


## What capabilities make real-time consolidation possible?


Four building blocks show up again and again in platforms that deliver this:


1.


**Multiple entities in one instance** (or continuous connectors into every ledger)


2.


**Shared or mapped account structures** so rollups do not wait on manual renaming


3.


**Intercompany workflows** (journals, bills, transfers, payment matching) so IC is posted cleanly at the source


4.


**Automated eliminations** that clear internal activity in the consolidated view as it posts


Miss any one, and “real time” degrades into “faster batch.” Shared masters ([shared master data in multi-entity accounting](https://www.liveflow.com/blog/shared-master-data-multi-entity-accounting) ) and disciplined[intercompany journal entries](https://www.liveflow.com/blog/intercompany-journal-entries-multi-entity-erp) are what keep the live view trustworthy.

## How to talk about this with your CFO or board


Frame the upgrade in outcomes, not features:


-


“We can answer consolidated margin questions mid-month without a fire drill.”


-


“Eliminations are rules in the system, not a fragile worksheet tab.”


-


“Entity and group views come from the same numbers.”


-


“Close still happens. We just stop using close as the only time the group exists.”


That language matches how operators experience pain, and it stays accurate to what one-instance ERPs and live FP&A layers actually deliver.


## Frequently asked questions


Questions teams ask about real-time multi-entity consolidation.


## What is real-time multi-entity consolidation?


It is the ability to view consolidated financials from live entity data, with eliminations applied, without waiting to rebuild a consolidation workbook after each period close.


## Does consolidating without close mean skipping month-end?


No. You still reconcile, review, and lock periods. Real-time consolidation separates management’s need for a current group view from the statutory close checklist.


## Can QuickBooks Online consolidate in real time across entities?


Not natively. Separate company files require exports or a connected consolidation/FP&A layer such as LiveFlow FP&A for live group reporting.


## Does Flow Agentic Accounting Platform support real-time consolidation and automated eliminations?


Yes. Flow Agentic Accounting Platform supports real-time consolidation and automated eliminations for multi-entity groups running in one instance, alongside intercompany journals, bills, transfers, and payment matching.
